title: Claude plugin inbound through the session inbox socket, as its own session puppet
description: Claude Code registers the sock channel only with --dangerously-load-development-channels and a dialog per launch, so plain claude sessions never hear the owner (MCP logs: not in --channels list). Claude Code hands every MCP server the session's inbox (CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET, CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN); a user line written there reaches the session (probe 2026-10-16, arrived as a peer message). sock-mcp --claude-inbound: the session's own puppet (ADR 3, Claude side of integrations-ad2) subscribes and each owner reply is written to the inbox and acked. Run lock, archive on exit, rename from custom-title, reconcile crashed sessions. Plugin switches from --channel to --outbound-only --claude-inbound; notify.sh sends as the session puppet.

title: Puppet per agent session, not per repository
description: Owner ruling 2026-10-15: one puppet per agent session (Claude Code CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, Codex thread id), display name from the session's name plus host and renamed on rename (UpdateDisplayName). Puppets are kept when the session ends and go inactive, shown in an Archived tab (client told, sock-client). Supersedes contract ADR 10's project naming; needs a hub inactive state and the 100-puppet cap revisited (server). Replaces the ask records, project matching and per-project listener in Codex inbound (integrations-2ol) and fixes integrations-fdh.

title: Codex inbound: a sock reply reaches the live Codex session
description: 2026-10-15: the Codex plugin is outbound only, so a reply to a message Codex sent goes nowhere. Candidates: (1) Codex's app-server: the TUI is a client of a local app-server over a unix socket (~/.codex/app-server-control, logs show rpc.transport=unix_socket, client codex-tui), and the binary has thread and turn start and steer requests, so a sock listener could inject the reply as a turn on the live thread. Unprobed. (2) sock-runner's codex exec resume per message: works headless, but resuming a thread the TUI holds open forks it. (3) Stop hook fetches pending messages and blocks with them as the reason: reaches the session only at a turn end, never while idle. Probe (1) first; design pass (DDD, contracts) before code.
notes:
Probe 2026-10-15, Codex CLI 0.162.1, daemon codex-tui/0.163.0: the TUI is a client of a per-user app-server daemon; ~/.codex/app-server-control/app-server-control.sock (symlink into /private/tmp/codex-daemon-<uid>/) speaks JSON-RPC over a WebSocket upgrade (codex app-server proxy passes raw bytes and does not frame). A second client: initialize {clientInfo}, initialized, thread/loaded/list (ids), thread/read (cwd, ephemeral, threadSource, status), then turn/start {threadId, input:[{type:text,text}]}. The live TUI showed the injected text as a user turn and Codex answered it there. Mid-turn, turn/start added the input to the active turn: Codex answered it then finished the original work. Pick the thread with matching cwd, ephemeral false, threadSource user (each TUI turn also loads an ephemeral thread_title thread with the same cwd). Without a thread subscription the client saw no turn notifications. Schema: codex app-server generate-json-schema.
Design pass 1: docs/specs/codex-inbound.md and docs/adr/0001. Also probed: a thread stays loaded after its TUI quits and turn/start runs a full turn unattended. Open: no-session policy, unattended approvals, thread/resume after reboot.
Built: sock-mcp 4dff1b2 (asks), integrations a59106e (hook asks), bab2ed5 (sock-codex, service codex-live), 46012ad/7f324a5 (injector), eaadb40 (review fixes), 10c3744. Live: sock-codex with real whoami gate injected into a scratch TUI; redelivery caught as duplicate from session history. Left: install the service for a real project and reply from the sock app (sock listen delivery not yet exercised); integrations-fdh blocks using it in a repo where Claude Code also runs with the channel.
ADR 2 (17:00): the plugin's sock-mcp listens (--codex-inbound, machine lock, cached puppets only, rescan on thread/started and idle); sock-mcp 7f46cbe 3b4b84b 2497dbc, sock-client 8629d50 (Projects.Cached), integrations cecfee3. Release needs sock-client v0.1.7 tagged and pushed and sock-mcp .client-ref bumped (make install builds pinned v0.1.6, which lacks Cached). Left: owner's live reply test.

title: Codex plugin sock-mcp dies in the plugin root with only a machine key

Codex shows no sock tools, so the model falls back to the sock CLI. Fix in sock-mcp: with a machine key under PLUGIN_ROOT, start anyway, declare the capability and resolve the project puppet per call from sandboxCwd (cached per dir), matching the hooks' sock send --as-puppet.

title: sock-mcp --channel acks owner replies in a session that has no channel registered
description: The plugin always runs sock-mcp --channel. A Claude Code session started without --dangerously-load-development-channels (or --channels) registers no channel and drops notifications/claude/channel, but sock-mcp writes the notification, counts that as pushed and acks, so the owner's reply is consumed and lost. Seen live 2026-10-14 (integrations-pvq). Fix: only consume when the client positively shows it registered the channel (find the signal in Claude Code's initialize request or docs), else leave deliveries pending and stay outbound plus tools.
notes: Fixed in sock-mcp v0.3.3 (chancap, sock-ops). Skill change merged into integrations main: a reply passes message_ids, sock_ack for messages needing no reply; Claude Code plugin 0.3.11. Closes with pvq once a channel-enabled session shows a reply arriving.

title: notify.sh: background sessions never message the owner; interactive asks throttled to one per project per hour
description: Owner got dozens of sock messages from agents overnight; says people would ignore or uninstall a tool that does that. Rule: background/headless/agent sessions never send (fail closed on unknown); interactive asks at most once per project per hour (permission prompts count); replies via sock_send untouched; nothing else sends.
close_reason: notify.sh gate: interactive only, one send per project per hour; live-checked quiet under claude -p and codex exec

title: Plugin hooks: say what the session needs, send nothing when nothing is pending, never repeat
description: Guy, 2026-10-13 via sock-client, from his phone: 'These messages are not helpful. Is something waiting on me, then tell me what I need to do in the sock message.' Today idle_prompt and Stop post fixed phrases ('<project>: waiting for you', 'finished a turn') through notify.sh. Wanted: when a session is waiting on him, the message carries the ask from the session's last assistant message (hook input last_assistant_message for Stop; the transcript tail for idle_prompt), trimmed to the question or decision, capped, code blocks dropped; when nothing is pending, nothing is sent (the notify_on_stop opt-in keeps 'finished a turn' for those who want it); the same pending ask is not reposted (hash of the ask kept per project in the state dir). permission_prompt forwards the Notification message, which names the tool. This reverses the v1 'fixed phrase, never transcript text' decision at the owner's request; the spec records why. Tests first in test/notify_test.go.
close_reason: Shipped 9e8a549 (plugin 0.2.0) and the security-review fixes in 3ae4e73: per-turn dedupe, no hash tool skips dedupe, token and secret-shape redaction, other fence shapes, text on stdin, regular-file and 2 MiB transcript fallback skipping tool-only entries. Not taken: an (agent) marker on the prefix, UTF-8-safe cut (valid in tests), double send under concurrent idle.

title: Claude plugin: several sessions on one machine share one puppet and compete for its deliveries
description: Seen 2026-10-13: the plugin is user-scoped, so every Claude Code session on the Mac runs sock-mcp --channel as the same puppet (MacM5Claude). A puppet token is one device with one delivery stream, so sessions compete for the owner's replies; the orchestrator session and this one both received or lost replies. The v1 assumption 'one puppet per machine' breaks for anyone running more than one session. Options: (a) per-session device tokens minted at sock-mcp startup (needs a minting capability the plugin token lacks: a sock-mcp or hub change), (b) hub-side fan-out to every connected device of a puppet (Messaging change, deliveries per device already exist), (c) a single-consumer election on the machine (lock file) so only one session's channel subscribes and the others are outbound-only, with the session that holds it named in sock_whoami. (c) is local and shippable now; (a) or (b) is the real fix. Decide with the hub team; spec first.
notes: Shipped: hook machine-key path (plugin 0.3.2), sock-cli v0.2.2 puppets ensure, sock-mcp v0.2.3 Codex fallback. Guy must verify (yje): sock machine-key create, set the plugin key, two repos give two puppets. Then close.

title: sock-mcp change: Claude Code channel is lost when the 2026-07-28 revision is negotiated
description: Corrected diagnosis (code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp#push-messages-with-channels, changelog 2.1.292 and 2.1.295): on Claude Code's v2 runtime a channel server that negotiates revision 2026-07-28 is NOT registered as a channel; a server on the earlier handshake is. Since 2.1.292 local stdio servers negotiate 2026-07-28 by default (MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION=legacy opts out). sock-mcp on go-sdk v1.8.0 accepts the new handshake, so Claude Code 2.1.296 lands on 2026-07-28 and shows: Channel messages from plugin:sock:sock are unavailable: this connection's protocol version has no channel delivery path for claude. Live-seen 2026-10-13 with puppet MacM5Claude; tools work, inbound does not. Workaround for users now: MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION=legacy in the environment of claude. Fix in sock/mcp: when --channel is set, offer protocol versions only up to 2025-11-25 so Claude Code falls back to the legacy handshake and registers the channel (find the go-sdk option or hook for the supported-version list); lift the cap when Claude Code's changelog adds channel delivery on 2026-07-28. Document the env workaround in claude-code/README.md meanwhile. Verify with an owner reply arriving as a channel tag.
notes: 2026-10-14 22:09Z live check: Guy replied in direct conversation 01a1384d (puppet sock-integrations); no channel tag arrived. Cause: this session runs 'claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --resume' without --dangerously-load-development-channels, so Claude Code registers no channel, yet the plugin's sock-mcp --channel (pid 20038, started 2026-10-13 20:44, binary since replaced; its sock_send description predates 47a5ab3) still pushes and then acks, so the owner reply is consumed unseen. Four sock-mcp --channel processes on the Mac (pluma, orchestrator spare, a claude -p haiku, this one), each its own project puppet. New bug filed for sock-mcp: never ack unless the client registered the channel. pvq stays open until a session started with the dev flag shows the tag.

title: Claude inbound: a cached session token the hub evicted is never re-checked until restart
description: security review 2026-10-16: claudeSession.For returns the cached client without Ensure, so after TOKEN_INVALID (evicted, revoked) both tools and listener fail until the session restarts. Replies wait at the hub, not lost. Fix: on a permanent TOKEN_INVALID from a call or the stream, drop the client and Ensure again (renews the token).

title: Session puppets: don't mint for non-interactive Codex threads
description: Security review 2026-10-15 finding 4: any Codex thread that makes one sock tool call or fires one hook mints a permanent session puppet, subagent and exec threads included. The listener never serves those (they are archived at once), and ADR 27 has no cap, so a prompt-injected session spawning subagents mints without bound. Options: ask the daemon on a thread's first call and mint only for interactive threads (fail open or closed when the daemon is absent, e.g. the desktop app); or send a subagent thread as its parent's puppet. Needs a decision.

title: Codex inbound: cap the age of a held reply
description: Security review 2026-10-15 (integrations-2ol): with no loaded Codex session the reply stays pending (owner decision 1). When a session appears, maybe days later on unrelated work, every held reply is injected into it, and a 'yes, go ahead' acts out of context. Option: sock-codex acknowledges and drops (or posts a notice for) a reply older than N hours instead of injecting it. Needs the owner's call on N and on drop vs notice.

title: Claude Code and Codex in one repo share a project puppet, so they compete for the owner's replies
description: Project puppets are per repository and host (ADR 10), not per platform. A Claude Code session with the sock channel on and a sock-codex runner service in the same repo both consume that puppet's deliveries (rule 2: one consumer per puppet), so a reply meant for Codex can land in Claude Code or the reverse. Found 2026-10-15 with a Codex TUI and a Claude Code session both in sock/integrations. Options: platform in the puppet name (<repo> on <host> via codex), or the runner service refuses to install while a channel session holds the puppet. Needs a design call.

title: Codex hook treats a headless codex exec resume of a TUI session as attended
description: Security review 2026-10-14, reproduced: notify.sh:346-353 trusts the rollout's first session_meta source (cli), which records how the session was created. codex exec resume appends no new session_meta (spec line 128), and SOCK_HEADLESS covers only sock-runner. So a cron job, script or a Bash tool running 'codex exec resume <tui-session>' sends to the owner. Repro: rollout first line {type:session_meta,payload:{id:S1,source:cli}}, input {session_id:S1,turn_id:t1,...,last_assistant_message:'Done. Ship it?'}, --stop --ask-now, no SOCK_HEADLESS: sock send runs. Fix needs a live Codex probe of the hook's process ancestry or another per-turn attended signal (exec vs TUI); needs a logged-in Codex, so parked until one is available in a throwaway CODEX_HOME.

title: Codex plugin route: hooks send with SOCK_TOKEN, the plugin's sock-mcp with config machine_key/puppet_token, so they can disagree or the hooks send nothing
description: Audit finding 3 (plugins.md). ADR 10 says hook and server always agree. With no env token notify.sh sends nothing; a bare sock send would use the human login token, so it cannot just fall back. Needs a sock CLI way to resolve the same credential sock-mcp resolves (SOCK_TOKEN, then machine_key with ensure, then puppet_token) for sock send. Coordinate with sock-ops.
notes: sock-cli v0.2.5 ships sock send --as-puppet [--project dir] (sock-client v0.1.1 ResolvePuppet, shared with sock-mcp v0.2.5). Refusals fixed text on stderr, exit 1. Hook: on the Codex plugin route (PLUGIN_ROOT set, no CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_SOCK_TOKEN) with no SOCK_TOKEN, send with --as-puppet --project "$PLUGIN_ROOT". Verified v0.2.5 still takes the hook's current SOCK_TOKEN + --url send. Wire after integrations-8lv lands (same file).

title: sock-mcp change: read the CLI config file (token, url, access_gate) when the environment has none
description: Lives in sock/mcp (no beads database there). Live check 2026-10-13 of the Codex plugin route (integrations-fwm): Codex starts a plugin's stdio MCP server with only PLUGIN_ROOT and PLUGIN_DATA in its environment, never the parent's SOCK_TOKEN, and the plugin mcp.json schema has static env only, so a plugin cannot forward the token by name and sock-mcp exits 'no token: set SOCK_TOKEN'. The sock CLI already keeps token, url and access_gate in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/sock/config.toml (mode 600 enforced). If sock-mcp falls back to that file when SOCK_TOKEN is unset, the plugin works with no secret in the plugin and one 'sock login' or config write per machine. Keep env precedence as today. Filed from the fwm live check.

title: sock-mcp change: flag to serve only the sending tools (outbound-only)
description: Lives in sock/mcp (that repo has no beads database, so tracked here). Integrations rule 2: a puppet has one consumer of its deliveries. Beside sock listen (runner/sock-runner) and in the Codex plugin, the agent must not see sock_fetch or sock_ack. Hosts enforce it unevenly: Claude via --allowedTools/--disallowedTools, Codex via config.toml enabled_tools, and the Codex plugin mcp.json has no tool filter at all. Add a sock-mcp flag such as --outbound-only that registers only sock_whoami, sock_list_conversations and sock_send; then the Codex plugin mcp.json passes it in args and the drift test pins the reduced set. Filed from the integrations-fwm review.

title: notify.sh: strip control chars before first redaction in detail path
description: Final review: notify.sh detail path redacts raw stderr before stripping control chars, then cuts to 300 bytes; a token split by a control byte can leak a short prefix. Fix: pipe head -c 65536 through tr -d cntrl before redaction. Needs sock stderr to echo the token, so near-zero real risk.
close_reason: Closed

title: sock CLI retries unavailable until killed
description: notify.sh hook measured: 'sock send' retries unavailable forever (3 requests in 2s, 5 in 12s) until the caller kills it. Hook has its own 10s watchdog so it is bounded, but the sock-cli owner should decide whether send needs an overall deadline. Found during integrations Task 1.
close_reason: Filed as sock-cli-84a in sock/cli

title: Hosted MCP surfaces: Responses API, claude.ai, ChatGPT, Managed Agents cloud
description: sock-mcp is stdio only. These need a public Streamable HTTP endpoint and an OAuth-style credential (Responses API takes an OAuth access token in the authorization field; sock_pt_ untested there). Multi-tenant token proxy and OAuth layer need a security review. Revisit with a real need.
notes:
2026-10-14 surfaces research (four agents, docs fetched live today; full notes were in session scratch).
All four surfaces are pull only toward Claude/agents except ChatGPT (MCP events, now at developers.openai.com/plugins/build/mcp-events; the apps-sdk/build/events URL 404s). OpenAI renamed apps/connectors to plugins.
Responses API + Agents SDK HostedMCPTool: bring-your-own bearer in `authorization`, no OAuth discovery/DCR/CIMD, no server requirements. Gap (ours): a way for a developer to mint and refresh a sock access JWT outside a platform; docs for allowed_tools and approval.
claude.ai/Desktop custom connectors + directory: OAuth with CIMD preferred (needs client_id_metadata_document_supported and none in token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported), redirect https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback, loopback for Claude Code, egress 160.79.104.0/21, PRM resource must equal the URL exactly. Directory needs a title plus readOnly/destructive hint on every tool, non-steering descriptions, privacy policy, docs page, reviewer test account. Messages API mcp_servers: bearer only.
ChatGPT: dev mode passed on staging. Directory needs all three hints explicit on every tool, domain challenge, org verification, legal pages, logo, 5+3 test cases, demo video, reviewer account without MFA; RFC 9207 iss lets ChatGPT use the stable redirect.
Managed Agents: mcp_servers url plus vault mcp_oauth credential (access, expires_at, refresh with none or client_secret_* auth, not private_key_jwt); Anthropic refreshes; no OAuth flow run by Anthropic; no inbound events into a session.
Ours: (a) every tool gets title and explicit readOnly/destructive/openWorld hints (sock-mcp tools); (b) connector.md events link and plugin terminology; (c) token helper for API and Managed Agents callers (bead); (d) hub metadata and redirect checks for Claude and RFC 9207 (sock server); (e) public docs, privacy, terms, support pages and review assets drafted (Guy approves).
Blocked on Guy: production hub OAuth enable (prod AS metadata 404s today); OpenAI org verification, challenge token into Render prod, submission; paid Claude account and directory submission with legal acks; Anthropic API key with Managed Agents billing; approve legal pages; a populated reviewer account with a non-Apple sign-in.

title: sock-bridge: Managed Agents session creation
description: Split from integrations-0ga. Create a session on first use (agent and environment from config) instead of requiring SOCK_BRIDGE_SESSION.
notes: Security review 2026-10-14 (scratchpad kzk-security.md): fix after 0ga lands on bridge-followups-2 (same file, same worktree). Rulings: M: Check also compares agent id, environment, pinned version and set budget with config; a mismatch replaces the session with the fixed notice 'the bridge configuration changed; this reply started a new session'. L1: Find adopts only on environment, pinned version and budget match too. L2: a 2xx create with an id the bridge refuses exits 2 with a fixed log line. L3: map_put fails closed when the sessions file cannot be read (check awk's status). L4: verify on the docs whether a budget ends a session (budget_reached is an idle stop reason, not terminated); record it in the spec.

title: sock-bridge follow-ups: owner-brokered tool confirmations, session creation, webhook delivery
description: Out of scope for the first bridge (integrations-xft spec): answer requires_action tool confirmations from a sock reply, create sessions, receive events over webhooks instead of a stream.
notes: Security review 2026-10-14 (scratchpad 0ga-security.md): no High or Medium. Rulings, fix after the kzk fixes land (same worktree): L1 and the design note: post the confirmation requests as their own message before the agent's text, so no cut can drop them and they are distinct from agent text. L2: scrub pending codes from a deny reason after removing format characters (Cf, including U+200B), case-insensitively. L3: an ordinary reply in any conversation has every pending code replaced with [code] before it goes into a session. L4: pass codes to awk and sed through ENVIRON, never argv. L5: never evict a sent line or a line from the current turn; calls past the bound are not asked and the owner is told to answer them in the console. L6: dedupe event_ids.
close_reason: Merged to main (rebased bridge-followups-2, tip 9871296), make check rc 0; two security reviews each. Live-API shape checks remain open (see notes).

comments.author: Guy J Grigsby
comments.text: Re-review 2026-10-14 (0ga-security.md) R1-R4, rulings: R1 fold fullwidth U+FF01..FF5E to ASCII and drop combining marks U+0300..036F before matching codes (matching only, text unchanged elsewhere); spacing and homoglyphs stay residual, recorded in spec. R2 drop the global Cf strip from deny reasons; the code pattern already tolerates format characters between letters. R3 one turn asks at most 20 calls; another session's pending lines are never evicted by a turn; when the file is full, new calls are not asked and the owner gets the console note. R4 sent lines count toward the 50 bound; a sent line older than 24 h is dropped. Fix after the kzk breaker lands (same worktree).
